label: paragraph_title
text: CANNON DISCOVERY

label: text
text: IRON AND BRONZE WEAPONS. BURIED IN SAND.

label: text
text: "On the island of Gili Genting," the entrance to the bay of Soemeng, writes a Madura correspondent to one of the local

label: text
text: mapers, a treasure lies partly buried in the shape of iron and bronze: annon, numbering from 200 to 00.

label: text
text: A Dutch artillery officer is now on the island superintending the work of digging out the cannon which have sunk into the sandy soil.

label: text
text: These guns were brought to the island by a British fleet in command of the then Governor-General, Sir Stamford Raffles, for the bombardment of Soemenep and the subjugation of the Sultan of that island.

label: text
text: Before operations were begun, however, the decree respecting the return of Java and the other islands to the Dutch was made. The fleet then sailed away, leaving the cannon behind.

label: text
text: An official controversy prevailed for a while respecting the ownership of the cannon, the Dutch claim being finally validated.

label: text
text: The cannon will be transported to Java and broken up, the metal representing a considerable value.

label: paragraph_title
text: SCENES AT FUNERAL.

label: text
text: A crowd of 300 angry wome chased a bereaved husband through the cemetery at Willesden, an pelted him with clods of earth.

label: text
text: He was Albert Putteney, whose wife, Mrs. Ada Kathleen Petchley, aged 27, and her two-year-old girl were found dead in a gas-filled room. At the inquest it was stated that the husband had left them two days previously without any money, and the jury asked the Coroner to ensure the husband.

label: text
text: Women tried to attack Petchley as he entered the mourning coach on leaving the house, but he was protected by the undertaker's men. At the cemetery the crowd booied and shouted and threw turf at Petchley, who was on the verge of collapse.

label: text
text: He walked from the carriage supported by his mother. Owing to the shouting of women the service was nearly inaudible, and at the end Petchley had to run from the cemetery, pursued by the crowd of women. He managed to get back to the coach, which was driven rapidly away.

label: paragraph_title
text: CHRISTIANITY.

label: text
text: CHINESE ARE FAILING TO ACCEPT.

label: text
text: Shanghai, China, Sept. 28.—The success of the Christian cause in China is not what most optimists have expected in the past few years. With the recent anti-foreign agitation and anti-Christian movement the Chinese have ceased to accept Christianity.

label: text
text: This is the uncompromising verdict of Rev. Arthur H. Smith, octogenarian, who spent 54 years in China and who is the author of numerous volumes on missionary work in the Orient. His views are supported by not a few of the leading secretaries now in the field. Those Americans, who have dug deep in their purses to convert Chinese are doubtless surprised but the bald statement of fact is probably true. Especially in those centres where foreign commercial men have been boycotted, has Christianity been barely able to hold its own.

label: text
text: The solution of the problem has been searched for by those at home in China—the enigma to date is unsolved.

label: text
text: As counter-irritant to student and atheist propaganda, leaders of the Christian movement have hit upon the plan of making the Oriental convert carry on. With this programme in full operation, leaders believe that the Church will come into its own again.—"United Press."

label: text
text: ATTEMPT TO LYNCH FATHER..

label: text
text: Vienna.—Several hundred people at Villach, in Carinthia, tried to lynch a railwayman named Modre, who, during a quarrel with his wife, flung their 10-years-old daughter. Therese from a second floor window when she attempted to separate them. The child fell upon her head and was instantly killed.

label: text
text: Gendarmerie had to protect the father with drawn swords. The man will be charged with murder.
